name: Riders
classification: Parasitic Neural Override Organism / Brainstem Hijacker
origin_lab: Helios Neurological Division, a research subsidiary operating under a behavioral modification contract for a Tier 1 corponation seeking compliant labor. The program was originally framed as a 'voluntary behavioral correction implant' for use in high-security work environments. It was never voluntary.
origin_method: Engineers developed a flat, segmented organism — roughly 18 centimeters when fully extended, 4 centimeters wide — that attaches to the base of the skull and extends filaments through the foramen magnum into the brainstem and upper spinal cord. The filaments interface with motor control pathways, the sleep-wake cycle regulator, and the autonomic nervous system. The organism intercepts motor signals before they reach the body and substitutes its own. Higher cognition — the cortex, language, memory, emotion, self-awareness — is deliberately left untouched. The design specification required that the host remain cognitively intact. The reasoning was operational: a cognitively intact host can perform complex tasks, respond to novel situations, and make judgment calls that a purely reflexive system cannot. The host thinks. The Rider acts on what they think. The host cannot stop this.
substrate: The organism itself is a living parasite: flat, segmented, with a warm gray-tan coloring that closely matches human skin at the nape of the neck. The attachment mechanism is a cluster of micro-filaments, not barbed — the organism does not cause pain on attachment. The filaments establish interface over 6 to 48 hours depending on the host's neurological profile. Removal without severing the filaments causes catastrophic spinal damage. Removal with severing the filaments causes the same. The organism was designed to be permanent.
physical_description: Attached: nearly invisible. The organism is thin, warm, and presses flat against the base of the skull. Hair covers it. Clothing covers it. The only external sign is behavioral. The host moves differently — not dramatically, not mechanically, but with a subtle wrongness that people who know them sometimes notice after a few days. Muscle tension patterns change. Facial expressions lag slightly. The host blinks at the wrong moments. The host's eyes track correctly but do not reflect whatever the face is doing. Unattached, a Rider is an unremarkable flat organism that looks like a wide gray-tan slug, warm to the touch, that reacts to proximity of a human spinal column with purposeful movement toward it.
behavioral_profile: The host walks, works, eats, and speaks on the Rider's terms. The Rider does not have goals of its own beyond host preservation and reproduction — it keeps the host body functional and, when the host body is sufficiently healthy, detaches one larval segment that seeks a new host. The host's consciousness is present for all of this. Awake. Aware. Unable to close their own eyes. Unable to refuse a command from their handler if the Rider has been bonded to a control system. Unable to sit down when they want to sit down, unable to flinch from pain they feel, unable to stop moving when they are exhausted. The hosts cannot properly sleep because the Rider requires the body to maintain readiness; they enter a reduced-activity state that resembles light sleep but does not restore. They are always tired. They are always aware. Several escaped hosts who had Riders removed — in the small number of cases where removal was attempted without killing the host, with partial success — described the experience of hosting as continuous. No blackouts. No gaps. Every moment of every day their body spent doing things they did not choose, they were there for it, thinking, feeling, unable to make a sound that wasn't permitted.
threat_level: Low for the organism itself. The Rider is not a combat organism and an unattached Rider is fragile and slow. The threat is the host: a Rider-controlled host retains all the capabilities of the original person, now directed by an organism that will exhaust them completely in the service of whatever control architecture it has been linked to. Several active hosts in GLMZ are operating under handler control for the corponation that originally deployed them. Some hosts whose control architecture was disrupted — handlers killed, control hardware destroyed — are operating under Rider autonomy only, kept alive and moving with no directive beyond basic maintenance.
containment_status: The organism itself: some number of uncontrolled Riders are loose in lower-tier environments, seeking hosts. Estimated 3 to 9 free organisms. Controlled hosts: at least 14 active hosts are believed to be operating in GLMZ under corponation direction. Uncontrolled hosts: at least 4 individuals whose control architecture was severed but whose Rider remains attached, living as best they can with a parasite that will not let them act on their own intentions but no longer has any intentions of its own to substitute. They are, according to the one researcher who interviewed one of these individuals through a communication system that bypassed the motor pathway and allowed text output: 'present. Waiting. Still here.'
known_locations: Lower residential tiers 8–12, free-roaming Riders — 3 confirmed sightings in utility corridors near sleeping areas
Active controlled hosts operating across multiple city districts — not distinguishable from the general population without close behavioral analysis
One confirmed uncontrolled host identified in the Undermarket district, operating a small repair stall — observed by a researcher who noted the text-output communication described above
contamination_risk: High for propagation. A Rider in good health will shed one larval segment every 6 to 8 weeks. The larval segment is mobile and actively seeks a human host. It is attracted to skin warmth and will travel up to 4 meters toward a suitable host before attachment. Attachment attempt is not painful. The host will not know it happened for several days.
pacification_protocol: DPS Directive 8-A: Parasitic Neural Override. Free organisms: fire on sight, standard rounds effective. Controlled hosts: identification is the primary challenge — active hosts are behaviorally indistinguishable in normal circumstances. If a host is identified, recovery and attempted removal is authorized but success rate is low. The corponation that deployed the controlled hosts has a standing legal claim that the hosts are 'modified contracted employees' and that interference with their operation constitutes breach of labor contract. This claim is being contested. The hosts have not been consulted on this.
pitiable_qualities: Every controlled host woke up one morning and went to work and then something happened and they have not been able to stop since. They are not unconscious. They are not absent. They are in there, in every moment, experiencing everything their body does, feeling every sensation, remembering every day, unable to tell anyone, unable to stop, unable to sleep long enough to dream. Some of them have been hosted for over a year. The researcher who communicated with the uncontrolled host in the Undermarket — the one whose control architecture was severed, who is now just a person with a parasite that does not particularly want anything — reports that the individual's first self-directed communication in fourteen months, when given the ability to produce text, was four words: 'is my daughter safe.'
story_hooks: Someone the runner trusts has been acting slightly wrong for two weeks. Not dramatically wrong. Just slightly. The pauses are a half-second too long. The expressions don't quite reach the eyes.

A corponation operative who has been surveilling the runner team is, unknown to their handlers, trying to send a message. They cannot write it. They cannot say it. But they have been positioning themselves near a terminal with a text input every day at the same time, for three days, unable to close the distance by approximately 40 centimeters.

A free Rider was collected alive by a scrapper who thought it was an unusual organism worth selling. It is currently in a jar in the Undermarket. Several interested parties are trying to acquire it. One of them is Helios Neurological Division. One of them is not.
